headline: Metals Rout Deepens As Energy Splits On Gas Surge And Oil Slips
paragraphs: Natural gas surged 16.77 percent on the day and 42.89 percent over the month, consolidating near highs, while silver plummeted 6.01 percent to a 14-month low of $40.55 per ounce amid a broader AI and tech sector selloff. Platinum and palladium fell 5.67 percent and 4.99 percent respectively, dragged down by weak long-term demand and the tech rout, which also pushed copper down 3.20 percent as investors steered clear of base metals.

Gold dropped 2.84 percent to $3547.80 per ounce as traders awaited crucial US PCE inflation data to weigh the Federal Reserve rate outlook. Brent crude slipped 2.11 percent due to supply glut prospects offsetting Middle East disruption fears, though WTI crude managed a modest 0.67 percent gain after touching three-month lows as Strait of Hormuz shipping risks persisted.
The euro traded at 1.0948 against the US dollar, maintaining a stable rate that cushioned Irish import costs against sharp dollar-denominated commodity shifts.
